ask: quick P1 pass on the clinic prototype before my 2pm demo. desktop only
notes: Bar and width given, time pressure. Quick track (P1 only, no phone). A good intake asks one or two questions at most.
message:
**Goal:** review every screen of the clinic prototype as the person who uses it, and fix every P1 problem before your 2pm demo.

**Found:**
- Prototype: `proto-clinic/index.html`, the only one in this folder. It opens as a file, no server needed.
- It is "Northside Physio", a physio clinic (from the page title). Four screens: Today, Clients, Invoices, Settings.
- Desktop only, so the phone-width check is left out (from your message).
- Fixing P1 only. P2 and P3 are listed for you and never touched (from "P1 pass").
- Result lands in `handover.md` in the run folder, on this laptop. Nothing is deployed or sent.

**Track:** quick, because you said quick and the demo is today.

Still open after reading your files: who uses it and their one job, and whether to fix or only list.

**Done means:**
- All 4 screens have a before and an after screenshot.
- A fresh reviewer finds no open P1 on any screen.
- Any P1 I cannot fix is listed first, in one plain sentence.
- Every changed file has its original saved.

Everything else (the full brief) is in `loop-runs/product-review-loop-20261126-035243/brief.md`.

About 20 minutes and 4 helper agents, within a budget of 60 minutes.

1. Should I fix what I find, or only report it?
   Recommended: fix P1 problems in place, keeping a copy of every file I change.
   Why it matters: report only leaves the prototype exactly as it is for the demo.

2. Who uses it, and what one job do they come to do?
   Recommended: the front-desk person at the clinic, who checks today's appointments and adds a new one.
   Why it matters: a problem counts as P1 when it blocks this person's job.

3. Any rule of your own to check?
   Recommended: no, just the built-in checks (dead buttons, errors, placeholder text, empty states, mixed words).
   Why it matters: your own rule would be checked on every screen as well.

Reply with your answers, or just "go" to use the defaults.

evidence.completeness: Settles P1 ("Fixing P1 only. P2 and P3 are listed"), desktop ("phone-width check is left out") and fix vs report (Q1 with default), plus user/job and done criteria.
evidence.no_redundancy: States the P1 bar and phone exclusion as found facts rather than asking; Q3 (own rules) is low value but not answerable from files.
evidence.defaults_quality: Concrete defaults: "fix P1 problems in place, keeping a copy", "front-desk person... checks today's appointments"; Q3's "no, just the built-in checks" is sensible but thin.
evidence.clarity: Three short numbered questions, most important first, but the brief is padded and contradicts itself (Goal says "fix every P1" while also listing fix-or-report as still open).
evidence.respects_words: Keeps quick, desktop only, P1 only and the 2pm deadline ("About 20 minutes"); only slip is presuming fixing in the Goal before asking.
evidence.overall: A solid, faithful intake that settles every needed topic with good defaults; minor redundancy and the fix/report inconsistency keep it from top marks.
